title: dedicated: autoscaler rollout + burst smoothing + utilization reporting improvements
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: customers on Dedicated fleets observed transient request queueing during traffic spikes which led to tail latency regressions. This PR implements a controlled rollout of the autoscaler smoothing logic, enhances token-bucket based burst controls to avoid oversubscription, and extends utilization reporting so SREs and customers can correlate burst allowance with observed throughput. Summary of changes: 1) Autoscaler rollout: add a rollout flag and staged canary policy so we can enable smoothing on a subset of fleets and capture metrics before global enablement. The rollout supports percentage-based enabling and per-fleet opt-outs. 2) Burst smoothing: replace the previous hard token refill with an exponentially-weighted refill that reduces large instantaneous token grants; this prevents short-term oversubscription on shared hosts while preserving queued throughput for legitimate bursts. 3) Throughput guarantees: add an explicit per-fleet throughput floor that the autoscaler attempts to maintain even under smoothing; this uses a short-window SLA estimator to avoid oscillation. 4) Utilization reporting: instrument token-bucket state, burst-granted tokens, and smoothed-requests-per-second in the observability pipeline (metrics + traces). Expose per-fleet and per-config dashboards. 5) Tests & rollout safety: add unit tests for the smoothing math and an integration test that runs a synthetic spike workload against a simulated fleet; add a fail-open path so if the rollout controller fails, fleets revert to previous behavior. Implementation details: the core smoothing is implemented in dedicated/autoscaler/smoothing.py as SmoothingController; token-bucket logic moved to dedicated/autoscaler/tokenbucket.py with clearer invariants and comments. The rollout controller (dedicated/rollout/controller.go) reads Linear flags and a configmap for percentage and per-fleet overrides. Observability hooks are in observability/metrics/dedicated_autoscaler.{proto,exporter}. Backwards compatibility: config defaults preserve current behavior (smoothing disabled) until rollout is bumped. Performance: measured in perf-canary with the canary fleet (see ENG-3241), showed 15-25% reduction in 99th percentile queueing latency for synthetic spikes with no throughput loss for steady-state traffic. Rollout plan: incremental enablement over 2 weeks, monitor new metrics and rollback on sustained latency increase > 5% over baseline.

release_notes:
- Add autoscaler smoothing with controlled rollout (disabled by default)
- Improve token-bucket burst controls to reduce oversubscription
- Add per-fleet throughput floor to maintain SLA under smoothing
- Expose new metrics: dedicated_autoscaler.burst_tokens, dedicated_autoscaler.smoothed_rps
- Add integration test for synthetic spike scenarios
extra_notes: Rollout: ops will increment canary percentage to 25% after 48 hours if canary metrics are stable; full rollout planned after 2 weeks. If >5% sustained tail latency regression is detected, ops will rollback the rollout flag. Linked support ticket SUP-9123 contains customer repro traces.
